prediction.likelyOutcome: Windsor is the likely net winner: its cost-to-complete counterclaim (roughly $25,000-$35,000) and the $3,960 lien-bond cost should survive termination-for-cause findings that are well-supported in the trial record, while Speedy's breach/unjust-enrichment claims (at most ~$21,700) are weak given documented underperformance and testimony that Windsor received no benefit from Speedy's work. The large wildcard is Windsor's slander-of-title claim for increased financing costs (quoted as 'over a million dollars'), which faces real malice and causation hurdles and should be heavily discounted, though it cannot be ignored entirely given the record.

issues.label: Windsor's Breach of Contract Counterclaim (Cost to Complete)

figures.label: Payment to Speedy for fifth-floor work that delivered no benefit
figures.quote: Although Windsor paid Speedy $44,300 to restore the fifth floor, it received no benefit from Speedy's work because everything had to be redone.

figures.label: Payment to Osorio to redo the fifth-floor work
figures.quote: Windsor paid Osorio a total of $65,300 for the work he completed on the fifth floor of the garage.

figures.label: Offset for original contract budget Windsor would have paid for competent performance
figures.quote: The budget for the project was $75,000 per floor of the garage, and the parties understood that to mean they were not to exceed $75,000.

issues.label: Speedy's Breach of Contract / Unjust Enrichment Claims

figures.label: Mechanics lien / claimed amount owed
figures.quote: Speedy filed a mechanics lien on the property for $66,000, which was recorded with the Montgomery County Recorder.

figures.label: Payments already made by Windsor
figures.quote: The total amount paid to Speedy by Windsor for this project was $44,300.

figures.label: Bond premium payments to discharge the lien
figures.quote: Windsor made two payments for a total of $3,960 to pay for the bond.

issues.label: Slander of Title — Increased Financing/Interest Costs
Defense: No Benefit Conferred (Defeats Unjust Enrichment)
Mechanics Lien Foreclosure — Mooted by Bond

outcome.description: After a two-day bench trial the court found for Windsor, awarded it $44,300 (the amount it had paid Speedy) plus prejudgment and postjudgment interest on its breach-of-contract counterclaim and $3,960 on its slander-of-title counterclaim (bond premiums), a total of $48,260, voided Speedy's $66,000 mechanics lien and denied Speedy's claims. The Second District affirmed.
